clue.text: Morris Bolter, put out to grass by Dickens

definitions.text: Morris Bolter, put out to grass by Dickens

parts.words: Morris Bolter, put out to grass by Dickens
parts.note: Morris Bolter is the alias taken in Oliver Twist by Fagin's recruit, the charity-boy undertaker's apprentice; a bolter is also a runaway horse, hence 'put out to grass'

explanation.surface: Dickens retires an old runaway horse called Morris Bolter to pasture.
explanation.definitionFit: In Oliver Twist the apprentice who bullies Oliver later calls himself Morris Bolter when he joins Fagin in London.

clue.text: He issued a summons to a topping event

definitions.text: He issued a summons to a topping event

parts.words: He issued a summons to a topping event
parts.note: a summons is an invitation and a topping is a beheading: the Russian-American novelist wrote Invitation to a Beheading

explanation.surface: Someone sends out invitations to a splendid party.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of Lolita also wrote the novel Invitation to a Beheading, and 'topping' is slang for execution.

clue.text: Margaret Mahy recorded more than one in the family

definitions.text: Margaret Mahy recorded more than one in the family

parts.words: Margaret Mahy recorded more than one in the family
parts.note: the New Zealand children's writer wrote ... in the Family, so she recorded more than one outsider there

explanation.surface: A children's author notes several relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahy's book title has the plural of this word for a stranger from another world.

clue.text: Making a meal of Lolita con?

indicators.note: making something of the given words means building a new word from their letters

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a swindle over Nabokov's novel is being made much of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making a meal of' reads as the idiom for over-fussing, but 'Making' signals the anagram and 'a meal' is the definition; 'of' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: A collation is a light meal, often cold, served informally.

clue.text: A privy Greek hero

definitions.meaning: Sir John Harington's Metamorphosis of ... punned on 'jakes', old slang for a lavatory
the warrior of the Trojan War who fought Hector

explanation.surface: A secretive Greek champion.
explanation.definitionFit: The name was an Elizabethan pun on jakes, a toilet, and also names a Homeric warrior.

clue.text: Gilbert's solitary game

definitions.meaning: the comic opera by Gilbert and Sullivan mocking aesthetes
the card game played alone, called solitaire in America

explanation.surface: W. S. Gilbert plays cards on his own.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta and the British name for one-player card games.

clue.text: The Hydra was keeper of its gate to the Underworld

definitions.text: The Hydra was keeper of its gate to the Underworld

parts.words: The Hydra was keeper of its gate to the Underworld
parts.note: the many-headed serpent killed by Heracles lived in a spring-fed lake in the Argolid said to be an entrance to Hades

explanation.surface: A monster guards a gateway to the land of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek site with its bottomless lake was where Heracles fought the serpent guarding a way into Hades.

clue.text: One of Dobson's rhymed offerings

parts.note: Austin Dobson, the Victorian poet

explanation.surface: A poet presents one of his rhyming verses.
explanation.definitionFit: Dobson's collection title names short descriptive sketches put into verse.

clue.text: Type of embrace encouraged by Mike Hammer

definitions.text: Type of embrace encouraged by Mike Hammer

parts.words: Type of embrace encouraged by Mike Hammer
parts.note: Mickey Spillane's private eye appears in Kiss Me, ..., so the embrace is a lethal kiss

explanation.surface: A tough detective urges a particular kind of hug.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spillane title invites a kiss described by this word for lethal.

clue.text: Very clever, like Williamson's porkies

definitions.meaning: porkies are lies (rhyming slang, pork pies); the Williamson title calls its lies dazzling

explanation.surface: A remark that someone's fibs are marvellously smart.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means outstandingly intelligent and also dazzling, the epithet in the Williamson title.

clue.text: Racine caught out author of English version of Andromache

definitions.text: author of English version of Andromache

indicators.note: out says a letter is put out of the playwright's name

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: The French tragedian is dismissed in a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes C from RACINE; the French playwright wrote Andromaque, which the poet Craig Raine adapted in English.
explanation.definitionFit: Craig Raine, the English poet, produced a version of Racine's tragedy about Hector's widow.

clue.text: "Three misbegotten knaves in —— green came at my back" (Henry IV, Part One)

definitions.text: "Three misbegotten knaves in —— green came at my back" (Henry IV, Part One)

parts.words: "Three misbegotten knaves in —— green came at my back" (Henry IV, Part One)
parts.note: Falstaff's tall tale of his attackers names a coarse green woollen cloth from a Westmorland town

explanation.surface: A line from Falstaff's boast about the robbers who set upon him.
explanation.definitionFit: Kendal green was a woodsman's cloth named after the town in the Lake District where it was woven.

clue.text: Won back, like Marcel's time

definitions.meaning: the last volume of Proust's novel is translated as Time ...

explanation.surface: Proust's narrator recovers lost time.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means recovered, and it is the English title word for Le Temps retrouvé.

clue.text: Associated with traveller by Lawrence

parts.note: D. H. Lawrence's novella The ... and the Gipsy pairs a young woman with a travelling man

explanation.surface: Lawrence links someone to a wanderer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawrence's title couples a chaste young woman with a Romany traveller.

clue.text: Frank disguise for Hamilton

parts.note: Charles Hamilton wrote the Billy Bunter stories as Frank ..., so 'Frank' is a first name, not candid

explanation.surface: An honest mask worn by someone called Hamilton.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Richards was the pen name of the prolific schoolboy-story writer Charles Hamilton.

clue.text: Mary, who bore a charmed life

definitions.text: Mary, who bore a charmed life

parts.words: Mary, who bore a charmed life
parts.note: the American novelist Mary of The Group also wrote the novel A Charmed Life

explanation.surface: A lucky woman named Mary.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of The Group published A Charmed Life in 1955.

clue.text: I hoped art might portray a daughter of Zeus

indicators.note: the letters might portray a new figure, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist hopes painting could depict a goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: The goddess of love is in one account Zeus's child by Dione.

clue.text: "Won't't do this time — you must try again, old " (Charlotte Smith, Marchmont)

definitions.text: "Won't't do this time — you must try again, old " (Charlotte Smith, Marchmont)

parts.words: "Won't't do this time — you must try again, old " (Charlotte Smith, Marchmont)
parts.note: a quotation from Charlotte Smith's novel in which a quibbling lawyer is addressed by an old term for a petty legal trickster

explanation.surface: A line from Charlotte Smith's novel brushing off a failed ploy.
explanation.definitionFit: To pettifog is to quibble over trifles, and a pettifogger is a shabby lawyer.

clue.text: It is exemplified in a letter of Lord Macaulay

definitions.text: It is exemplified in a letter of Lord Macaulay

parts.words: It is exemplified in a letter of Lord Macaulay
parts.note: a letter here is a written character: the l and d of 'Lord' rise above the line, not a piece of correspondence

explanation.surface: Something is illustrated in correspondence from the historian.
explanation.definitionFit: In typography the stroke rising above the x-height in letters like l, d and h has this name.

clue.text: Associated with discussions by Chesterton

parts.note: G. K. Chesterton's essay collection is ... and Discursions

explanation.surface: Chesterton links something to debate.
explanation.definitionFit: Chesterton's title pairs warnings of danger with rambling talks.

clue.text: Forster awarded a couple to democracy

definitions.text: Forster awarded a couple to democracy

parts.words: Forster awarded a couple to democracy
parts.note: E. M. Forster's essay collection is Two ... for Democracy

explanation.surface: A novelist hands out a pair of prizes to the democratic system.
explanation.definitionFit: Forster's title gives democracy two shouts of approval rather than the customary three.

clue.text: American novelist detained among offspring

indicators.note: among puts one piece within the other

parts.note: a son is a male offspring
detained means held

explanation.surface: An American writer is locked up with the children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offspring' looks plural, suggesting children in general, but one son is enough; Sidney Sheldon wrote bestselling thrillers.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidney Sheldon was an American author of popular thrillers such as The Other Side of Midnight.

clue.text: Some fatal antagonist in race for gold

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A deadly opponent turns up in a contest for first prize.
explanation.walkthrough: The heroine lost her footrace to Hippomenes, who distracted her with golden apples, so 'in race for gold' defines her.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek huntress stopped mid-race to pick up golden apples and so lost the contest.

clue.text: Psalmist starts a song as poetic hymn

indicators.note: starts tells us to take the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A psalmist begins a song in the manner of a poetic hymn.
explanation.definitionFit: Asaph, a Levite musician of David's court, is credited with twelve of the Psalms.

clue.text: Identity of Robert Ludlum

parts.note: Ludlum's thriller The ... Identity gives its amnesiac spy this surname

explanation.surface: A question of who the thriller writer really is.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludlum's novel title puts this surname before the word Identity.

clue.text: That of truth explored by Santayana

definitions.text: That of truth explored by Santayana

parts.words: That of truth explored by Santayana
parts.note: George Santayana's ... of Being includes the volume The ... of Truth

explanation.surface: A philosopher investigates a domain of truth.
explanation.definitionFit: Santayana's volume title names a domain or kingdom of truth.

clue.text: Press club

definitions.meaning: to smooth clothes with a heated appliance
a golf club with an angled metal head

explanation.surface: A newspaper association.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to smooth fabric and also names a metal-headed golf club.

clue.text: Greek murderess exposed in Persian article

parts.note: a Mede was one of the ancient people who ruled Persia with the Persians
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A killer from Greece is revealed in a Persian object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposed in' only links; the Medes are the ancient Iranian people of 'the Medes and Persians'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Euripides the sorceress kills her own children to punish Jason.

clue.text: The Duenna's Don

parts.note: Sheridan's comic opera The Duenna has a Spanish gentleman, Don ..., among its lovers

explanation.surface: A chaperone's Spanish gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Don Ferdinand is one of the young lovers in Sheridan's opera The Duenna.

clue.text: Donleavy finally asked for mercy on this wild one (3)

definitions.text: Donleavy finally asked for mercy on this wild one (3)

parts.words: Donleavy finally asked for mercy on this wild one (3)
parts.note: J. P. Donleavy's riotous novel about the dissolute Sebastian Dangerfield in Dublin

explanation.surface: An author at last begs for leniency for a wild character.
explanation.definitionFit: J. P. Donleavy's first novel follows a red-haired roistering American student in Dublin.
